  1515			\text{\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-2b}} &\approx_{\eps} \sum_{\substack{g,h: \\ (\coded(g)-h)\cdot \tilde{u} = a}} (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \cdot \Big((M^{(\Point,W),u}_{(g-g_h)(u)})_{\alice} \otimes (\tau_h^W)_{\alice''} \Big) \cdot \Big ( M^{(\Point,W),u}_{(g-g_h)(u)} \Big)_{\bob} \label{eq:qld-pulling-3} \\
  1660		\leq& O(\delta_S + \eps).
  1661	\end{align*}
  1662	\Cref{eq:qld-sg-cons2} is thus obtained by absorbing $\eps$ into the function $\delta_S$.  
  1663	\end{proof}
  1664		
  1665	
  1666	 The next lemma shows that we can construct local unitaries $V_A,V_B$ from the measurements $\hat{S}$  such that the shared state $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$ is close to $\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$ for some state $\ket{\aux}$, and the observables $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$ are mapped to Pauli observables $\tau^W(e_j \tilde{u})$ acting on $\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$. Using the consistency between the $\{\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a\}_{a \in \F_q}$ measurements and the points measurements $\{M^{(\Point,W),u}_a\}_{a \in \F_q}$ established in \Cref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}, and the consistency between the points measurements and the ``total Pauli measurements'' $\{M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h\}_{h \in \F_q^\nqubits}$ established in \Cref{lem:qld-win-implications}, we deduce that the total Pauli measurements must be close (up to the local unitaries $V_A,V_B$) to the Pauli projectors $\{\tau^W_h\}_{h \in \F_q^\nqubits}$ acting on $\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$.
  1667	
  1668	
  1669	\begin{lemma}
  1670	\label{lem:qld-unitary}
  1671	There exists a function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)$ (where $\delta_S$ is defined in \Cref{lem:qld-4-7}) and unitaries $V_\alice$ acting on registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ and $V_\bob$ acting on $\bob \bob' \bob''$ such that 
  1672	\begin{enumerate}
  1673		\item There exists a state $\ket{\aux}$ on registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ such that
  1674		\[
  1675			\left \| V_\alice \otimes V_\bob \ket{\hat{\psi}}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''} - \ket{\aux}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\alice'' \bob''} \right \|^2 \leq \delta_\qld.
  1676		\]
  1677		
  1678		\item For all $W \in \{X,Z\}, h \in \F_q^\nqubits$
  1679		\begin{align*}
  1680			V_\alice \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \Big)_{\alice} \, V_\alice^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \\
  1681			 V_\bob \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h  \Big)_{\bob}\, V_\bob^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''}
  1682		\end{align*}
  1683		where the $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\aux}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\alice'' \bob''}$. 
  1684	\end{enumerate}
  1685	\end{lemma}
  1686	
  1687	\begin{proof}
  1688	
  1689	Define the linear map
  1690	\[
  1691		V_\alice = \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)))_{\alice ''}\;,
  1692	\]
  1693	where the $\tau^X(\cdot),\tau^Z(\cdot)$ act on $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$. (Also note that the argument of $\tau^X$ is $\coded(g_Z)$ and the argument of $\tau^Z$ is $\coded(g_X)$.) We verify the unitarity of $V_\alice$:
  1694	\begin{align*}
  1695		V_\alice V_\alice^\dagger &= \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) )_{\alice ''} \\
  1696		&= \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Id_{\alice ''} \\
  1697		&= \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}
  1698	\end{align*}
  1699	where in the first line we used that the measurement $\{ \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \}$  is projective and in the second line we used that the $\tau^Z$ and $\tau^X$ observables are self-inverse. The unitary $V_\bob$ is defined analogously.
  1700	
  1701	Let $\{e_j\}_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}}$ denote the self-dual basis for $\F_q$ over $\F_2$ specified in \Cref{sec:subfields}, and let $\tilde{W}^j$ be the observables introduced in~\eqref{eq:def-tildewj}. Conjugating the observable $\tilde{W}^j$ acting on the registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ by the unitary $V_\alice$ we get
  1702	\begin{align*}
  1703		&V_\alice \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_\alice^\dagger \\
  1704	  =& \sum_{g_X, g_Z} (-1)^{\tr( e_j(\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \\
  1705	  &\hspace{24em}\tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\alice ''} \\
  1706		 =& \sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\alice ''} \\
  1707		 =& \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\alice ''}\;,
  1708	\end{align*}
  1709	where in the third line we used the (anti-)commutation relation
  1710	\[
  1711		\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = (-1)^{\tr( e_j(\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \;.
  1712	\]
  1713	An entirely analogous calculation shows that $V_\bob \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_\bob^\dagger = \Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \Big( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\bob ''}$.
  1714	
  1715	Next, from the self-consistency property of the observables $\tilde{W}^j$ specified in \Cref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} we get that for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1716	\[
  1717		\E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \left ( \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id - \Id \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \right)^\dagger \left ( \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id - \Id \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \right) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \leq \delta_S\;,
  1718	\]
  1719	which, since $\tilde{W}^j$ is Hermitian, is equivalent to
  1720	\begin{equation}
  1721	\label{eq:qld-unitary-1}
  1722	\E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \geq 1 - \delta_S/2\;.
  1723	\end{equation}
  1724	Let $\ket{\vartheta} = V_\alice \otimes V_\bob \ket{\hat{\psi}}$, and for $W \in \{X,Z\}$ define the operator
  1725	\begin{align*}
  1726		H_W &= \E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \otimes \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \\
  1727			&= \E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \Big ( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(e_j s) \otimes \tau^W(e_j s) \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits} \\
  1728			&= \Big ( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(s) \otimes \tau^W(s) \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits}
  1729	\end{align*}
  1730	where in the second line we used that for all $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$, $\tau^W(\tilde{u}) = \bigotimes_{i = 1}^\nqubits \tau^W(\tilde{u}_i)$ with $\tau^W(\tilde{u}_i)$ being the generalized Pauli $W$ observable acting on the $i$-th qudit. In the third line, we used the fact that for every fixed $j$, we have $\E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(e_j s) \otimes \tau^W(e_j s) = \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(s) \otimes \tau^W(s)$. \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-1} is then equivalent to 
  1731	\[
  1732		\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - \delta_S/2\;,
  1733	\]
  1734	for $W \in \{X,Z\}$. 
  1735	
  1736	Observe that
  1737	\begin{align*}
  1738		\E_{s,s'} \tau^X(s) \tau^Z(s') \otimes \tau^X(s) \tau^Z(s') &= \E_{s,s'} \sum_{a,b \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(as')} \ketbra{a+s}{a} \otimes (-1)^{\tr(bs')} \ketbra{b+s}{b} \\
  1739		&= \E_{s} \sum_{a\in \F_q} \ketbra{a+s}{a} \otimes \ketbra{a+s}{a} \\
  1740		&= \proj{\EPR_q}
  1741	\end{align*}
  1742	where to go from the first to the second line we used \Cref{lem:cancellation}. This implies that $H_X H_Z = \Big ( \E_{s,s' \in \F_q} \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') \otimes \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits} = \ketbra{\EPR_q}{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$.
  1743	By the triangle inequality, we have
  1744	\[
  1745		\left \| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\| \leq \left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_X \ket{\vartheta} \right\| + \left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\|\;.
  1746	\]
  1747	Note that for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1748	\[
  1749		\left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_W \ket{\vartheta} \right\|^2 = 1 - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} + \bra{\vartheta} H_W^2 \ket{\vartheta} \leq 2 - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} \leq \delta_S\;,
  1750	\]
  1751	where in the inequality we used that $H_W \leq \Id$. Furthermore,
  1752	\begin{align*}
  1753		\bra{\vartheta} H_W^2 \ket{\vartheta} &=\| H_W \ket{\vartheta} \|^2\\
  1754		 &= \| \ket{\vartheta} + (H_W - \Id) \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \\
  1755		 &\geq (\|\ket{\vartheta}\| - \| (H_W - \Id) \ket{\vartheta} \|)^2 \\
  1756		 &\geq (1 - \delta_S)^2 \\
  1757		 &\geq 1 - 2\delta_S\;. 
  1758	\end{align*}
  1759	Therefore 
  1760	\begin{align*}
  1761	2\sqrt{\delta_S} &\geq \left \| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\|^2  \\
  1762	&= \bra{\vartheta} H_X^2 \ket{\vartheta} + \bra{\vartheta} H_Z^2 \ket{\vartheta} - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_X H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \\
  1763	&\geq 2 - 4\delta_S - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_X H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \;,
  1764	\end{align*}
  1765	which implies that 
  1766	\[
  1767		\bra{\vartheta} (\Id_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes (\proj{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''}) \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - 2\delta_S - \sqrt{\delta_S} \;.
  1768	\]
  1769	Define the unnormalized state $\ket{\aux_0}$ on the registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ as
  1770	\[
  1771		\ket{\aux_0}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} = (\bra{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''} \cdot \ket{\vartheta}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''}
  1772	\]
  1773	and define the normalized state $\ket{\aux} = \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \ket{\aux_0}$. 
  1774	The inner product between $\ket{\vartheta}$ and $\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$ can thus be evaluated as
  1775	\begin{align*}
  1776		\bra{\vartheta} (\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}) &= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \bra{\vartheta} (\ket{\aux_0} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}) \\
  1777		&= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \bra{\vartheta} (\Id_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes (\proj{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''}) \ket{\vartheta} \\
  1778		&= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|^2 \\
  1779		&= \| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \| \\
  1780		&\geq \sqrt{1 - 2\delta_S - \sqrt{\delta_S}} \\
  1781		&\geq 1 - O(\sqrt{\delta_S})\;.
  1782	\end{align*}
  1783	This implies $\| \ket{\vartheta} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$, which establishes the first item of the lemma.
  1784	
  1785	We now establish the second item of the lemma. In what follows, all $\simeq$ and $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$. From \Cref{lem:qld-win-implications} we have the following implications: for all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and on average over $u \in \F_q^m$,
  1786		\begin{align}
  1787		\label{eq:qld-unitary-2}
  1788		M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} &\simeq_\eps \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a\;, \\
  1789		\label{eq:qld-unitary-3}
  1790		\Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a &\simeq_\eps  M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''}\;,
  1791		\end{align}
  1792		where $M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h$. 
  1793	From \Cref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} we get that
  1794		\begin{equation}
  1795		\label{eq:qld-unitary-4}
  1796			M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \simeq_{\delta_S} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}  \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a\;.
  1797		\end{equation}
  1798	Using \Cref{fact:triangle-for-simeq} with Equations \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-2}, \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-3}, and \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-4}, we get 
  1799		\begin{equation}
  1800			\label{eq:qld-unitary-5}
  1801			M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \simeq_{\sqrt{\delta_S}} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}  \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a\;,
  1802		\end{equation}
  1803		where we used that $\delta_S \geq \eps$. 
  1804		
  1805		Next, we have for all $u \in \F_q^m$ 
  1806		\begin{align}
  1807			&V_\bob \, \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \, V_\bob^\dagger \notag \\
  1808			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W_{g_W(u) - a}(\ind_m(u))    \tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1809			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a} \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W_h   \tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1810			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a} \Big ( \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)}   \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1811		= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} \Big ( \tau^W_{h}   \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1812	= &\Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]})_{\bob''}\;,		\label{eq:qld-unitary-6}
  1813		\end{align}
  1814		where in the second line we expanded out the definitions of $V_\bob$ and $\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a$ (defined in \cref{eq:tilde_M}); in the third line we expanded out the definition of $\tau^W_{g_W(u) - a}(\ind_m(u))$ (defined in \cref{eq:def-tauwu}) and used the fact that for all $h \in \F_q^M$, the inner product $h \cdot \ind_m(u)$ is equal to $g_h(u)$; in the fourth line we used the identities
  1815		\[
  1816			\tau^X(s) \tau^Z_h \tau^X(s)^\dagger = \tau^Z_{h + s} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \tau^Z(s) \tau^X_h \tau^Z(s)^\dagger = \tau^X_{h + s}~;
  1817		\]
  1818		and in the fifth line is due to the following short calculation: for all fixed $g_W$ we have
  1819		\begin{align*}
  1820			\sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a}  \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h: g_W(u) - g_h(u) = a} \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h: g_W(u) + g_h(u) = a} \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h': g_{h'}(u) = a} \tau^W_{h'}~.
  1821		\end{align*}
  1822		The second equality from the fact that $\F_q$ is a field of characteristic $2$ (so subtraction is the same as addition), and the third equality follows from the fact that letting $h' = h + \coded(g_W)$, we have $g_{h'} = g_h + g_W$ (in other words, the low-degree encoding $h \mapsto g_h$ is linear in $h$). 
  1823		
  1824		
  1825	
  1826	
  1827	Let $\ket{\Delta} = \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$. We show that $V_\alice \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \Big)_{\alice} \, V_\alice^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''}$ (the argument for the operators acting on registers $\bob \bob' \bob''$ proceeds identically). 
  1828		\begin{align}
  1829			&\sum_h \bra{\Delta} \left ( V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''}  \right)^\dagger \left ( V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \right) \ket{\Delta} \notag \\
  1830			&= 2 - 2 \Re \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice\, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \ket{\Delta} \notag \\
  1831			&= 2 - 2 \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-7}
  1832	\end{align}
  1833		where in the last line we used that $(\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} = (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$.
  1834		We now claim that
  1835		\begin{align}
  1836		&  \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta}  \notag \\
  1837		&\approx_{md/q}  \E_u \sum_{\substack{h, h' : \\ g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)}} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-8} \\
  1838		&=  \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \, V_\alice^\dagger \, \otimes (\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \notag \\
  1839		&=  \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \, V_\alice^\dagger \, \otimes V_\bob  \, \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \, V_\bob^\dagger \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-9}
  1840		\end{align}
  1841		where the equality in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-9} follows from the identity in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-6}, and the approximation in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-8} follows from the following calculation:
  1842		\begin{align*}
  1843			& \E_u \sum_{\substack{h \neq h' : \\ g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)}} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta}  \\
  1844			&= \sum_{h \neq h'} \left( \E_u \mathbf{1}[g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)] \right) \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \\
  1845			&\leq \frac{md}{q}\;.

   158	noncomputable def tildeObs {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}

   160	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P)
   161	    (j : Fin P.model.basisDim) : Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side)) :=

   163	    phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (P.model.basis j * a)) •

   171	private theorem sum_phaseSign_tauDotProj_sub {params : AdmissibleParams}

   173	    (coefficient offset : PauliScalar params) :
   174	    (∑ value : PauliScalar params,
   175	      phaseSign (fixedBinTrace params.model (coefficient * value)) •

   177	      phaseSign (fixedBinTrace params.model (coefficient * offset)) •

   179	  classical

   216	theorem tildeObs_eq_heteroKron {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}

   218	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P)
   219	    (j : Fin P.model.basisDim) :
   220	    tildeObs w side W u j =

   280	theorem tildeObs_isHermitian {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}

     4	/-! # Polynomial decoding for Pauli extraction
     5	
     6	This module provides the Chapter 16 decoder on the Chapter 15 bounded
     7	polynomial representative type.  The generic retained-value decoder and its
     8	specialization to polynomial representatives live in
     9	`Algebra/LowDegreeCodeTheorems`; this module states the corresponding maps on

    12	## References
    13	
    14	The decoder is blueprint `def:decoding-map`, with its extraction use in
    15	blueprint `sec:separating` and paper
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1419-1450`.
    17	The restricted decoder identity and its encoding hypothesis are documented in
    18	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`.
    19	-/

    21	open scoped BigOperators
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

    25	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

    27	/-! ## Representative evaluation and decoding -/

    29	/-- Evaluate the polynomial representative carried by `Poly P`.
    30	
    31	This is polynomial evaluation on the source's `\ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)` carrier.  It
    32	does not identify representatives that induce the same polynomial function. -/
    33	noncomputable def evalPoly {P : AdmissibleParams} (g : Poly P)
    34	    (x : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) : PauliScalar P :=
    35	  MvPolynomial.eval x g.1
    36	
    37	/-- Decode a bounded polynomial while retaining only values in `H`.
    38	
    39	This is the `H`-parameterized form of `def:decoding-map`; `decodeAt` remains
    40	the decoding map for arbitrary functions.  The Boolean cube is embedded in
    41	`PauliScalar P` by `cubeEmbed`. -/
    42	noncomputable def decodeOn {P : AdmissibleParams}
    43	    (H : Finset (PauliScalar P)) (g : Poly P) : PauliRegister P :=
    44	  decodeAt H (fun x => evalPoly g x)
    45	
    46	/-- Full-field specialization of `decodeOn` used in Chapter 16.
    47	
    48	The retained-value set is `Finset.univ`, so every field value is kept.  This
    49	choice is the correction recorded in
    50	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`. -/
    51	noncomputable abbrev decodeOnUniv {P : AdmissibleParams} (g : Poly P) :
    52	    PauliRegister P :=
    53	  decodeOn (Finset.univ : Finset (PauliScalar P)) g
    54	
    55	/-- The full-field decoder `\operatorname{Dec}_{\F_q}` on `Poly P`.

     6	
     7	This module encodes the Boolean subcube by multilinear indicator polynomials

    10	## References
    11	
    12	The source-facing nodes are blueprint `def:polynomials-degree`,
    13	`def:low-degree-encoding`, and `def:indicator-vector`; the paper origin is
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    15	The polynomial class `def:polyfunc` is reused from
    16	`MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc` (the LDT formalization).
    17	
    18	Note: this module contributes declarations to the comparator statement closure
    19	of the QPBT headline theorems, which must elaborate in the same environment as
    20	the Mathlib-only `ChallengeQPBT.lean`.  Keep the full `import Mathlib`; do not

    24	open scoped BigOperators
    25	open MvPolynomial
    26	
    27	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    28	
    29	/- The Boolean cube indexes the `2^m` qudits in the low-degree encoding. -/
    30	/-- The Boolean cube indexing the `2^m` qudits of the test.  This is the index
    31	type in blueprint
    32	`def:low-degree-encoding`, paper origin
    33	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    34	-/
    35	abbrev Cube (m : ℕ) := Fin m → Bool
    36	
    37	/--
    38	The representative polynomial which is `1` at `y` on the Boolean cube and
    39	zero at the other cube points.  This is the indicator polynomial in blueprint
    40	`def:low-degree-encoding`; paper
    41	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    42	-/
    43	noncomputable def indicatorPoly {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ} (y : Cube m) :
    44	    MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    45	  ∏ i : Fin m, if y i then X i else (1 - X i)
    46	
    47	/--
    48	The multilinear low-degree encoding of a coefficient string.  Polynomial
    49	representatives are used, as fixed by issue #0004, rather than quotienting by
    50	functional equality.  Blueprint: `def:low-degree-encoding`; paper origin:
    51	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    52	-/
    53	noncomputable def lowDegreeEncoding {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    54	    (a : Cube m → K) : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    55	  ∑ y : Cube m, a y • indicatorPoly y
    56	
    57	/- Evaluation shorthand for the representative polynomial in
    58	`def:low-degree-encoding`; it is Lean-only notation. -/
    59	/-- Evaluation shorthand for the low-degree encoding.  Blueprint
    60	`def:low-degree-encoding`, paper origin
    61	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    62	-/
    63	noncomputable def lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    64	    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) : K :=
    65	  eval x (lowDegreeEncoding a)
    66	
    67	/--
    68	The indicator vector `ind_m(x)` of `def:indicator-vector`.
    69	Blueprint: `def:indicator-vector`; paper origin:
    70	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    71	-/
    72	noncomputable def indicatorVec {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    73	    (x : Fin m → K) : Cube m → K :=
    74	  fun y => eval x (indicatorPoly y)
    75	
    76	/--
    77	The defining dot-product identity for the encoding, corresponding to
    78	Equation `eq:low-degree-encoding-definition` and `def:indicator-vector` in the
    79	blueprint, with source node `def:indicator-vector`; paper origin
    80	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    81	-/
    82	theorem lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    83	    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) :
    84	    lowDegreeEnc a x = dotProduct a (indicatorVec x) := by
    85	  simp [lowDegreeEnc, lowDegreeEncoding, indicatorVec, dotProduct]
    86	
    87	/--
    88	The coordinatewise product form of an entry of the indicator vector: at a cube
    89	point `y` the entry is the product of `x i` over the coordinates with `y i`
    90	true and of `1 - x i` over the remaining ones.  Blueprint
    91	`def:indicator-vector`;
    92	paper origin: `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    93	-/
    94	theorem indicatorVec_apply_eq_prod {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    95	    (x : Fin m → K) (y : Cube m) :
    96	    indicatorVec x y = ∏ i : Fin m, if y i then x i else 1 - x i := by
    97	  simp [indicatorVec, indicatorPoly, apply_ite]
    98	
    99	/--
   100	Over a commutative ring of characteristic two, the inner product of two
   101	indicator vectors is the product of the coordinate sums `1 + x_i + z_i`.  This
   102	is the product expansion of blueprint
   103	`def:indicator-vector`; it is the first step of
   104	the proof of blueprint
   105	`fact:omega-anticomm-prob`, paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:70-95`.
   107	-/
   108	theorem sum_indicatorVec_mul_indicatorVec {K : Type*} [CommRing K]
   109	    [CharP K 2] {m : ℕ} (x z : Fin m → K) :
   110	    ∑ y : Cube m, indicatorVec x y * indicatorVec z y
   111	      = ∏ i : Fin m, (1 + x i + z i) := by
   112	  have h2 : (2 : K) = 0 := CharTwo.two_eq_zero
   113	  have hfac : ∀ i : Fin m,
   114	      ∑ b : Bool, ((if b then x i else 1 - x i) * (if b then z i else 1 - z i))
   115	        = 1 + x i + z i := by
   116	    intro i
   117	    have h1 :
   118	        ∑ b : Bool, ((if b then x i else 1 - x i) * (if b then z i else 1 - z i))
   119	          = x i * z i + (1 - x i) * (1 - z i) := by
   120	      rw [Fintype.sum_bool]
   121	      simp
   122	    rw [h1]
   123	    linear_combination (x i * z i - x i - z i) * h2
   124	  calc ∑ y : Cube m, indicatorVec x y * indicatorVec z y
   125	      = ∑ y : Cube m, ∏ i : Fin m,
   126	          ((if y i then x i else 1 - x i) * (if y i then z i else 1 - z i)) := by
   127	        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   128	        intro y _
   129	        rw [indicatorVec_apply_eq_prod x y, indicatorVec_apply_eq_prod z y,
   130	          ← Finset.prod_mul_distrib]
   131	    _ = ∏ i : Fin m, ∑ b : Bool,
   132	          ((if b then x i else 1 - x i) * (if b then z i else 1 - z i)) := by
   133	        rw [Finset.prod_univ_sum, Fintype.piFinset_univ]
   134	    _ = ∏ i : Fin m, (1 + x i + z i) := Finset.prod_congr rfl fun i _ => hfac i
   135	
   136	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    34	\section{Key theorem forms}
    35	
    36	Let $e_0,\ldots,e_{t-1}$ be the fixed self-dual basis of $\mathbb F_q$ over
    37	$\mathbb F_2$.  With the phase convention of the source, generalized Pauli
    38	observables satisfy
    39	\[
    40	  \tau^X(a)\tau^Z(b)
    41	  =(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}(a\mathbin{\cdot}b)}
    42	   \tau^Z(b)\tau^X(a).
    43	\]
    44	Substituting $a=e_j\widetilde u$ and $b=e_{j'}\widetilde v$ gives the exact
    45	relation
    46	\[
    47	  \widetilde X^j(\widetilde u)\widetilde Z^{j'}(\widetilde v)
    48	  =(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}
    49	      (e_je_{j'}(\widetilde u\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde v))}
    50	   \widetilde Z^{j'}(\widetilde v)\widetilde X^j(\widetilde u).
    51	\]
    52	This formula applies uniformly, whether or not $j=j'$.
    53	
    54	\section{The false dichotomy in the source}
    55	
    56	Lines~1438--1450 of
    57	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
    58	identify each extracted observable with a tensor product containing
    59	$\tau^W(e_j\widetilde u)$.  Lines~1451--1456 then claim that the extracted
    60	$X$- and $Z$-observables commute whenever $j\neq j'$
    61	\cite[lines~1438--1456]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  Self-duality gives only
    62	\[
    63	  \operatorname{tr}(e_je_{j'})=0 \qquad (j\neq j').
    64	\]
    65	It does not imply
    66	\[
    67	  \operatorname{tr}(e_je_{j'}s)=0
    68	  \qquad\text{for every }s\in\mathbb F_q.
    69	\]

    72	pairing is nondegenerate, so there is an $s\in\mathbb F_q$ for which

    74	and $s$, with all remaining coordinates zero, gives

    31	  interpolant is elementary polynomial algebra.  The non-encoding-mass bound
    32	  uses project-specific consistency estimates and Schwartz--Zippel.
    33	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Multilinear interpolation on the
    34	  Boolean cube, injectivity of the low-degree encoding, measurement
    35	  consistency, and Schwartz--Zippel.  The correction is tracked in
    36	  \ghissue{19}.
    37	\end{itemize}
    38	
    39	\section{Key theorem forms}
    40	
    41	For a word $h\colon\{0,1\}^m\to\mathbb F_q$, let $g_h$ be its multilinear
    42	extension.  Define the chapter's decoder by
    43	\[
    44	  \operatorname{Dec}(g)(y)=g(y),
    45	  \qquad y\in\{0,1\}^m.
    46	\]
    47	Then
    48	\[
    49	  \operatorname{Dec}(g_h)=h
    50	  \quad\text{and}\quad
    51	  \operatorname{Dec}(g_h)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_m(u)=g_h(u).
    52	\]
    53	More generally, the second identity holds for a polynomial outcome $g$ under
    54	the explicit hypothesis that $g$ belongs to the image of the encoding; no
    55	converse is asserted.
    56	
    57	For an arbitrary bounded individual-degree polynomial $g$, the Boolean values
    58	determine its multilinear interpolant, not necessarily $g$ itself.  The
    59	unrestricted identity
    60	\[
    61	  \operatorname{Dec}(g)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_m(u)=g(u)
    62	\]
    63	is therefore false.
    64	
    65	\section{Counterexample and source comparison}
    66	
    67	The low-degree encoding is defined at lines~873--897 of
    68	\path{references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex}.  The general decoder at
    69	lines~917--924 retains evaluations lying in a chosen subset $H$; the extraction
    70	chapter instead specifies at lines~1419--1420 of
    71	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex} that the
    72	decoder returns all evaluations on the Boolean cube.  This is the specialization
    73	$H=\mathbb F_q$, rather than the Boolean-valued shorthand used earlier
    74	\cite[lines~873--924 and 1419--1420]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
    75	
    76	Take $m=1$, $d\geq2$, and a field of characteristic two with more than two
    77	elements.  For $g(x)=x^2$, the Boolean evaluations are $g(0)=0$ and $g(1)=1$.
    78	Consequently the decoder is the word whose multilinear extension is $x$.
    79	For any $u\notin\{0,1\}$ with $u^2\neq u$,
    80	\[
    81	  \operatorname{Dec}(g)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_1(u)=u
    82	  \neq u^2=g(u).
    83	\]
    84	Thus the equality asserted for every $g$ at lines~1483--1492 of the chapter-14
    85	source mirror is false \cite[lines~1483--1492]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  If degrees at
    86	least $q$ are allowed, equality as a function would not by itself prove encoding
    87	membership either, since $x^q$ and $x$ induce the same function on $\mathbb F_q$.
    88	In particular, $(q,m,d)=(8,1,2)$ is an admissible tuple exhibiting the
    89	failure: $1$ divides $8$, the extension degree is odd, and $d\geq1$.
    90	The polynomial reindexing used at lines~1805--1822 also fails here.  Set
    91	$h=0$ and $h'=h+\operatorname{Dec}(g)$.  Then $g_{h'}=x$, whereas the
    92	printed assertion $g_{h'}=g_h+g$ gives $x^2$.  These are unequal polynomial
    93	representatives, independently of the choice of evaluation point.
    94	
    95	\section{Required repair}
    96	
    97	The extraction proof must split the marginal measurement into encoding and
    98	non-encoding outcomes.  On encoding outcomes, the restricted identity above
    99	justifies the substitution.  On the complement, the proof must bound
   100	\[
   101	  \sum_{g\ \mathrm{not\ an\ encoding}}
   102	  \langle\widehat\psi,\widehat S_g^W\widehat\psi\rangle.
   103	\]
   104	For a supplied global polynomial-pair witness with point-consistency error
   105	$\delta_G$, the formal proof derives an
   106	$O(\delta_G+\sqrt\eps)+md/q$ bound. Measure the original Pauli answer $h$ and
   107	the ancillary ideal Pauli answer $h'$ and return $g_{h+h'}$. This reference
   108	measurement is supported on encodings. Perfect ancillary consistency and the
   109	Pauli-basis check bound its evaluated inconsistency with the marginal.
   110	A non-encoding polynomial differs from every encoded polynomial, so
   111	Schwartz--Zippel bounds the probability that their evaluations coincide.
   112	Completeness and positivity bound the non-encoding mass by the full polynomial
   113	inconsistency. This uniform estimate holds for both player sides; it is not
   114	inserted as an extraction hypothesis.
   115	
   116	The printed reindexing at lines~1805--1822 replaces
   117	$g_{\operatorname{Dec}(g_W)}$ by $g_W$, which is the invalid reverse identity
   118	for an arbitrary polynomial outcome.  In the corrected calculation, the
   119	constraint is
   120	$g_h(u)=\operatorname{Dec}(g_W)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_m(u)-a$.
   121	After setting $h'=h+\operatorname{Dec}(g_W)$, the defining evaluation formula
   122	$g_k(u)=k\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_m(u)$ and characteristic two turn
   123	that constraint into $g_{h'}(u)=a$.  Thus this step uses neither decoder
   124	linearity nor the identity $\operatorname{Dec}(g_h)=h$
   125	\cite[lines~1805--1822]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   126	
   127	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
   128	
   129	Definition~\path{def:qld-full-field-decoder} and
   130	Lemmas~\path{lem:qld-decoder-linearity} and
   131	\path{lem:qld-decoder-evaluation} in
   132	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex} state the full-field
   133	decoder, its linearity and inverse, and the evaluation identity restricted to
   134	encoding outcomes.  Lemma~\path{lem:qld-nonencoding-mass-bound}
   135	separately records the estimate on the remaining outcomes.
   136	
   137	The declarations \path{decodeFq_add}, \path{decodeFq_smul}, and
   138	\path{decodeFq_lowDegreeEncoding} in
   139	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Decoding.lean} match the three algebraic assertions.
   140	In the same file, \path{IsEncoding} is the equality
   141	$g_{\operatorname{Dec}(g)}=g$ of polynomial representatives, and
   142	\path{decodeFq_dotProduct_indicatorVec} requires an explicit hypothesis
   143	of that predicate.  It therefore matches the corrected evaluation lemma and
   144	does not assert the false unrestricted identity.  Finally,
   145	\path{nonencodingMarginalMass_le} in
   146	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/Consistency.lean} states one uniform theorem for
   147	the complementary mass bound on either player side.  It derives the bound from
   148	the projective strategy and global polynomial-pair witness rather than adding it
   149	as a witness field or theorem hypothesis.
   150	
   151	The decoder calculations are proved.  \path{lowDegreeEncoding_mem_poly},
   152	\path{decodeFq_add}, \path{decodeFq_smul}, \path{decodeFq_lowDegreeEncoding},
   153	and \path{decodeFq_dotProduct_indicatorVec} carry complete proofs: the degree
   154	side-condition on $g_h$, the two linearity laws, the inversion
   155	$\operatorname{Dec}_{\mathbb F_q}(g_h)=h$, and the evaluation identity under the
   156	explicit \path{IsEncoding} hypothesis.  The declarations
   157	\path{tildeM_consistent_pointMeas_ofGlobalPairWitness} and
   158	\path{tildeM_consistent_pointMeas'_ofGlobalPairWitness} prove the two specialized
   159	non-encoding estimates used by the pulled-apart point comparisons.  Each combines
   160	an encoding-supported reference comparison with the corresponding
   161	Schwartz--Zippel estimate, and \path{exists_pulled_apart_consistency} applies both
   162	results to one constructed global witness.  The uniform auxiliary theorem
   163	\path{nonencodingMarginalMass_le} is proved at its unchanged
   164	supplied-witness statement. Its proof uses the reference comparison and
   165	Schwartz--Zippel from
   166	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/NonencodingSupport.lean}; it is not called by that
   167	source-facing composition. The global witness constructor
   168	\path{exists_globalPairWitness} and the source-facing
   169	\path{exists_pulled_apart_consistency} are separately proved, including at
   170	zero error. This does not remove the witness premise from the auxiliary
   171	theorem. Issue~\#19 owns the Stage~4.2 statements and this discrepancy
   172	record; \ghissue{47} tracks the non-encoding support theorem, completed for a
   173	supplied witness by issue~\#517.
   174	No unrestricted decoder identity was asserted, and no residual assumption or
   175	additional witness field was introduced.
   176	
   177	\section{Retention and sufficiency of the correction}
   178	
   179	The two printed identities are retained separately as unasserted propositions.
   180	One quantifies over every bounded polynomial $g$ and every field point $u$ and
   181	states $\operatorname{Dec}(g)\cdot\operatorname{ind}_m(u)=g(u)$.
   182	The other quantifies over every bounded polynomial $g$ and every word $h$ and
   183	states $g_{h+\operatorname{Dec}(g)}=g_h+g$ as an equality of polynomial
   184	representatives.  Neither includes an encoding hypothesis.  They must not be
   185	identified: the example $g(x)=x^q$ satisfies the first identity at every point
   186	but violates the second at $h=0$.\footnote{The definitions are
   187	\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.PrintedDecoderEvaluationClaim} and
   188	\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.PrintedDecoderReindexingClaim} in
   189	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/PrintedClaims.lean}, tracked in
   190	\ghissue{667}.  They have no proofs and are not inputs to any consumer.}
   191	
   192	The consumer comparison distinguishes three calculations in the source.
   193	For point consistency at lines~1483--1492, both player orientations separate
   194	encoding outcomes from their complement.  The restricted evaluation identity
   195	applies only in the first sum, and the proved non-encoding estimate bounds the
   196	second.  The source-facing construction supplies one global measurement and
   197	applies both comparisons to it.  The separately stated uniform support estimate
   198	still takes a global measurement as a premise; its proof is not an
   199	unconditional construction and is not used by that composition.
   200	
   201	For observable self-consistency at lines~1495--1605, the difference polynomial
   202	$g-g_h$ has decoder $\operatorname{Dec}(g)-h$.  Consequently equality of two
   203	such polynomials gives equality of their decoded labels.  This uses only
   204	linearity and the left-inverse law $\operatorname{Dec}(g_h)=h$, both valid for
   205	the full-field decoder, and requires no encoding condition on $g$.
   206	The corresponding difference-polynomial and observable estimates are proved
   207	separately from the non-encoding estimate.\footnote{The algebraic identity and
   208	its use are \path{decodeFq_pullingPoly},
   209	\path{pulling_label_eq_of_poly_eq}, and
   210	\path{tildeObs_selfConsistent_ofGlobalPairWitness}.  The inverse law is also
   211	used by the encoding-supported reference and by the overlap transfer; these
   212	uses apply it only to an encoded word.}
   213	
   214	Finally, the swap-conjugation calculation at lines~1805--1822 uses the exact
   215	cancellation already described, not either retained false proposition.
   216	The ensuing unitary extraction and both final soundness conclusions therefore
   217	receive the same operator identities.  This covers the uses in the blueprint
   218	consistency, swap-conjugation, unitary-extraction, and soundness nodes as well
   219	as the two direct substitutions in the paper.
   220	
   221	The repair does not change the decoder specified at lines~1419--1420 or discard
   222	any polynomial outcomes.  The encoding restriction is a hypothesis of the
   223	local identity only, not of the extraction theorem.  No condition $d<q$ is
   224	added: when the collision estimate $md/q$ is large the support bound may be
   225	uninformative, but it remains valid.  Nor is encoding membership claimed to be
   226	necessary for pointwise equality at high degree.
   227	
   228	The additional consistency terms do not weaken the source error family.  Write
   229	$\delta_G=a(md)^a(\eps^b+q^{-b}+2^{-bmd})$ for the global-measurement error.
   230	For $0\leq\eps\leq1$, $md\geq1$, and $0<b\leq1/2$, one has
   231	$\sqrt\eps\leq\eps^b$ and $md/q\leq(md)^a q^{-b}$.
   232	Thus $C(\delta_G+\sqrt\eps+md/q)$ is absorbed by choosing the universal
   233	constants before the parameters and strategy, exactly as the source absorbs
   234	these terms after its pulling calculation.  The fourth-root extraction rate
   235	and the final soundness error family are unchanged, including at zero
   236	error.\footnote{The existing declarations \path{deltaExtract_le_deltaQld} and
   237	\path{exists_extractionWitness_fourth_root_rate} perform the downstream
   238	absorption; \path{exists_globalPairWitness} constructs the measurement.
   239	The source-law and tensor-code questions remain separate in
   240	\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex}.}
   241	This is a restriction of an invalid intermediate substitution, with its omitted
   242	contribution estimated, not a restriction of the source conclusion.  Independent
   243	hard review
   244	\href{https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/pull/672#pullrequestreview-5270109079}%
   245	{5270109079} verified all four adoption conditions, and main adopted this
   246	correction in
   247	\path{results/telemetry/source-adoptions-672-20260922.md}.  The retained
   248	propositions themselves remain unasserted and supply no proof evidence.
   249	
   250	\section{Conclusion}
   251	
   252	The decoding identity is false for a general polynomial outcome.  Restricting
   253	it to the encoding image is a necessary local correction.  The two specialized
   254	non-encoding-mass estimates required for the pulled-apart point-consistency
   255	conclusion are proved and used in the source-facing construction. The uniform
   256	auxiliary estimate is also proved for a supplied global witness, but the
   257	source-facing construction does not depend on it.

   822	\begin{remark}
   823	  \label{rmk:tm_fields}
   824	  Throughout this paper, whenever we refer to Turing machines that perform

   832	\subsection{Polynomials and the low-degree code}
   833	\label{sec:ld-encoding}
   834	
   835	In this section, we introduce some basic definitions about polynomials over finite fields. 
   836	An $m$-variate polynomial $f$ over $\F_q$ is a function of the form
   837	\[
   838		f(x_1,\ldots,x_m) = \sum_{\alpha \in \{0,1,\ldots,q-1\}^m} c_\alpha
   839	  x_1^{\alpha_1} \cdots x_m^{\alpha_m}
   840	\]
   841	where $\{c_\alpha\}$ is a collection of coefficients in $\F_q$.
   842	We say that $f$ has \emph{individual degree (at most) $d$} if $c_\alpha\neq 0$ only if
   843	$\alpha_i \leq d $ for all $1\leq i\leq m$, and that it has \emph{total degree
   844	  (at most) $d$} if $c_\alpha\neq 0$ only if $\sum_i \alpha_i \leq d$.
   845	(Affine) \emph{multilinear} polynomials are polynomials with individual degree
   846	$1$.
   847	
   848	Low-degree polynomials play an important role in this paper.
   849	For one, the classical and quantum low-degree tests of \Cref{sec:ldt} are
   850	nonlocal games that efficiently certify that the players' answers are consistent
   851	with low-degree polynomials.
   852	Low-degree polynomials are also crucial in the probabilistically checkable
   853	proofs (PCP) construction that are used in ``answer reduction'' transformation
   854	(\Cref{sec:ans}).
   855	
   856	We recall the Schwartz-Zippel lemma: 
   857	
   858	\begin{lemma}[Schwartz-Zippel lemma~\cite{Sch80,Zip79}]
   859	  \label{lem:schwartz-zippel}
   860	  Let $f, g: \F_q^m \to \F_q$ be two unequal polynomials with total degree at most $d$. Then
   861	  \begin{equation*}
   862	    \Pr_{x \sim \F_q^m}[f(x) = g(x)] \leq d/q\;.
   863	  \end{equation*}
   864	\end{lemma}
   865	
   866	
   867	\paragraph{The low-degree code.}
   868	The Schwartz-Zippel lemma implies that the set of low-degree polynomials form an
   869	error-correcting code with good distance, which we call the \emph{low-degree
   870	  code}.\footnote{It is also known as the \emph{generalized Reed-Muller code} in
   871	  the coding theory literature.}
   872	
   873	Fix an integer $m \in \N$ and let $M = 2^m$.
   874	For every $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ define the following $m$-variate multilinear
   875	polynomial over $\F_q$:
   876	\[
   877		\ind_{m,y}(x) = \prod_{i: y_i = 1} x_i \cdot \prod_{i: y_i = 0} (1 - x_i) \;.
   878	\]
   879	Here, we identify $\{0,1\}$ as a subset of $\F_q$.
   880	Notice that, when restricted to the subcube $\{0,1\}^m$, $\ind_{m, y}$ is zero
   881	everywhere except for when $x = y$.
   882	For $a\in \F_q^M$, label the coordinates of $a$ as $a_y$ for $y\in \{0,1\}^m$
   883	(identifying the latter set with $\{1,\ldots,M\}$ using, say, the lexicographic
   884	ordering on strings).
   885	For any such $a$ define the multilinear polynomial $g_a: \F_q^m \to \F_q$,
   886	called the \emph{low-degree encoding of $a$}, as follows:
   887	\begin{equation}
   888	\label{eq:ld-encoding}
   889		 g_a(x) = \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} a_y \cdot \ind_{m,y}(x)\;.
   890	\end{equation}
   891	Note that for any $y \in \{0,1\}^m$, $g_a(y) = a_y$.
   892	Furthermore, the map $a\mapsto g_a$ is linear: for every $x \in \F_q^m$,
   893	\begin{equation}
   894	\label{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}
   895		g_a(x) = a \cdot \ind_m(x)\;,
   896	\end{equation}
   897	where $\ind_m(x)$ is the vector $(\ind_{m,y}(x))_{y \in \{0,1\}^m}\in\F_q^M$.
   898	
   899	\begin{lemma}
   900	\label{lem:ld-encoding-complexity}
   901	Let $q$ be an admissible field size, and let $M = 2^m$ for some integer $m$.
   902	The complexity of computing the evaluation of the low-degree encoding $g_a(x)$,
   903	given $a \in \F_q^M$ and $x \in \F_q^m$ represented in binary, is $\poly(M,\log
   904	q)$.
   905	\end{lemma}
   906	\begin{proof}
   907		Computing $g_a(x)$ requires computing the sum of products $a_y \cdot
   908	  \ind_{m,y}(x)$ over all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$.
   909	  Via \Cref{lem:efficient_arithmetic}, evaluating $\ind_{m,y}(x)$ takes time
   910	  $\poly(m,\log q)$ because it requires performing $m$ multiplications of $\F_q$
   911	  elements, and therefore the product $a_y \cdot \ind_{m,y}(x)$ requires
   912	  $\poly(m,\log q)$ time.
   913	  Computing the sum over all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ requires $M \cdot \poly(m,\log q)
   914	  = \poly(M,\log q)$ time, as claimed.
   915	\end{proof}
   916	
   917	Finally, for any $H \subseteq \F_q$ we define the \emph{decoding} map
   918	$\coded_H(\cdot)$ which takes as input a polynomial $g : \F_q^m \to \F_q$ and
   919	returns the following vector $a \in \F_q^M$: for all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$, if $g(y)
   920	\in H$, then set $a_y = g(y)$, and otherwise set $a_y = 0$.
   921	Note that for all $a \in H^M$ we have $\coded_H(g_a) = a$ where $g_a$ is the
   922	low-degree encoding of $a$.

blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:15:The classical low individual degree game is a two-player game based on the low individual degree variant of the multilinearity test of Babai, Fortnow, and Lund. In the basic version, one player (the ``points player'') receives a uniformly random point $u \in \F_q^m$ and answers with a value $a \in \F_q$, while the other player (the ``lines player'') receives a random line through $u$ --- either axis-parallel or diagonal --- and answers with a univariate polynomial describing the restriction of a global function to that line. If the players share a polynomial $g\colon \F_q^m \to \F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$ and answer with $g(u)$ and with the restriction $g|_\ell$, they win with probability $1$; the soundness theorem below states that the converse approximately holds. In the simultaneous version, the players' answers are $k$-tuples, checked coordinatewise against a $k$-tuple of low individual degree polynomials.

blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:1388:The Pauli basis test is the quantum low individual degree test of Natarajan and Vidick, in the slightly modified form introduced by Natarajan and Wright~\cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}. Informally, the test certifies that the players share the state $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$, where $M = 2^m$. On a question of type $(\mathsf{Pauli}, W)$ with $W \in \{X,Z\}$, a player is expected to measure the generalized Pauli basis POVM $\{\tau^W_h\}_{h \in \F_q^M}$ of Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra} and report the outcome $h$. Most subtests probe limited information about $h$: given a point $u_W \in \F_q^m$, a player is expected to report the evaluation $g_h(u_W)$ of the low-degree encoding $g_h$ of $h$, and for a fixed basis $W$ these probes are checked against each other by the classical low individual degree game of Section~\ref{sec:ld-verifier}. Consistency \emph{between} the two bases is checked through two-outcome probes: given additionally $r_W \in \F_q$, a player reports $\tr(g_h(u_W)\, r_W) \in \F_2$. The two binary measurements obtained in this way for $W = X$ and $W = Z$ either commute or anticommute, according to the value $\gamma \in \F_2$ of Equation~\eqref{eq:gamma-value} below. When $\gamma = 0$ the verifier checks commutation directly by asking for both bits simultaneously; when $\gamma = 1$ the verifier checks anticommutation by playing the Magic Square game, using Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}.

   371	\begin{definition}[Individual and total degree]\label{def:polynomials-degree}
   372		\uses{def:polyfunc}
   373		An $m$-variate polynomial $f$ over $\F_q$ is a function of the form
   374		\[
   375			f(x_1, \dots, x_m) = \sum_{\alpha \in \{0, 1, \dots, q-1\}^m}
   376			c_\alpha\, x_1^{\alpha_1} \cdots x_m^{\alpha_m}
   377		\]
   378		with coefficients $c_\alpha \in \F_q$; the coefficients are uniquely
   379		determined by $f$, since the $q^m$ monomial functions indexed by
   380		$\alpha \in \{0, 1, \dots, q-1\}^m$ span the $q^m$-dimensional space of all
   381		functions $\F_q^m \to \F_q$ and are therefore linearly independent. The
   382		polynomial $f$ has \emph{individual degree (at most) $d$} if
   383		$c_\alpha \neq 0$ only when $\alpha_i \le d$ for all $1 \le i \le m$, and
   384		\emph{total degree (at most) $d$} if $c_\alpha \neq 0$ only when
   385		$\sum_i \alpha_i \le d$. (Affine) \emph{multilinear} polynomials are those
   386		of individual degree $1$.
   387		% Relationship to def:polyfunc: polyfunc keeps polynomial representatives,
   388		% so evaluation identifies it with the function classes above only for
   389		% d <= q-1.
   390		Definition~\ref{def:polyfunc} introduces the set $\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ of
   391		polynomials in $\F_q[x_1, \dots, x_m]$ of degree at most $d$ in each
   392		variable, identified by their polynomial representatives rather than by the
   393		functions they induce. Evaluation maps $\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ onto the set of
   394		$m$-variate polynomials of individual degree at most $\min(d, q-1)$ in the
   395		sense above; for $d \le q-1$ this map is a bijection, while for $d \ge q$
   396		distinct representatives, such as $x_1^q$ and $x_1$, induce the same

   398		representative convention of Definition~\ref{def:polyfunc}.

    29	/-- Source-facing construction for `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, paper
    30	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1463-1480`, using

    32	global measurements satisfies both point-consistency conclusions and observable
    33	self-consistency. The witness is an output, and all constants precede the

    41	with the three supplied-witness estimates. All estimates use the same witness,

    46	theorem exists_pulled_apart_consistency :
    47	    ∃ a b C : ℝ, 1 < a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧ 1 ≤ C ∧
    48	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon : ℝ),
    49	        0 ≤ epsilon → epsilon ≤ 1 → ∀ S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon,
    50	          ∃ w : GlobalPairWitness S (deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q),
    51	            ∀ W : PauliKind,
    52	              consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
    53	                  (fun u r => S.placePlayer .alice ((S.pointMeas .alice W u).effect r))
    54	                  (fun u r => S.placeSide .bob (tildeM w .bob W (indicatorVec u) r))
    55	                  S.psiHat ≤ deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon
    56	                    (deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q) P.m P.d P.q ∧
    57	              consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
    58	                  (fun u r => S.placeSide .alice (tildeM w .alice W (indicatorVec u) r))
    59	                  (fun u r => S.placePlayer .bob ((S.pointMeas .bob W u).effect r))
    60	                  S.psiHat ≤ deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon
    61	                    (deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q) P.m P.d P.q ∧
    62	              ∀ j : Fin P.model.basisDim,
    63	                opDistSq (uniformDistribution (PauliRegister P))
    64	                    (fun u => S.placeSide .alice (tildeObs w .alice W u j))
    65	                    (fun u => S.placeSide .bob (tildeObs w .bob W u j))

    67	                      (deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q) P.m P.d P.q := by

    71	  obtain ⟨C_obs, _, hobs⟩ := tildeObs_selfConsistent_ofGlobalPairWitness
    72	  let C := max (max C_AB C_BA) C_obs
    73	  have hAB_C : C_AB ≤ C := by
    74	    exact (le_max_left C_AB C_BA).trans (le_max_left (max C_AB C_BA) C_obs)
    75	  have hBA_C : C_BA ≤ C := by
    76	    exact (le_max_right C_AB C_BA).trans (le_max_left (max C_AB C_BA) C_obs)
    77	  have hobs_C : C_obs ≤ C := le_max_right (max C_AB C_BA) C_obs
    78	  refine ⟨a, b, C, ha, hb, hb_one, hC_AB.trans hAB_C, ?_⟩

    81	  have ha_nonneg : 0 ≤ a := by linarith
    82	  have hdelta : 0 ≤ deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q := by
    83	    simp only [deltaQld, Real.rpow_eq_pow]
    84	    positivity
    85	  have hscale : 0 ≤ deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q + Real.sqrt epsilon +
    86	      ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ) / (P.q : ℝ) := by
    87	    positivity
    88	  have hmono (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≤ C) :
    89	      deltaConstructPaulis c epsilon (deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q)
    90	          P.m P.d P.q ≤
    91	        deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon (deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q)
    92	          P.m P.d P.q := by
    93	    unfold deltaConstructPaulis
    94	    exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hc hscale
    95	  refine ⟨w, fun W => ⟨?_, ?_, fun j => ?_⟩⟩
    96	  · exact (hAB P epsilon _ hepsilon hepsilon_one hdelta S w W).trans
    97	      (hmono C_AB hAB_C)
    98	  · exact (hBA P epsilon _ hepsilon hepsilon_one hdelta S w W).trans
    99	      (hmono C_BA hBA_C)
   100	  · exact (hobs P epsilon _ hepsilon hepsilon_one hdelta S w W j).trans
   101	      (hmono C_obs hobs_C)
   102

    72	              (deltaExtract C (deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q)

    75	  obtain ⟨C₀, hC₀, hextract⟩ := exists_extractionWitness_ofGlobalPairWitness

1	# Completion protocol — definition of done
     2	
     3	Normative. This protocol says when a formalization **track** may be declared
     4	finished, and forbids the declaration until a model-free gate agrees. Amend it
     5	only through `local/protocols/meta.md` (`EVOLUTION.md` entry, cited trigger).
     6	
     7	Trigger for its existence, owner, 2026-09-19: *"some protocol(s) in the
     8	workflow should ensure that when the project finishes, the formalization is
     9	done without caveat, and satisfies the lean comparator"*; earlier the same day,
    10	*"i want zero sorry"*.
    11	
    12	## 1. Scope
    13	
    14	A **track** is a Lean subtree, the blueprint chapters describing it, its
    15	paper-gap register, its axiom-audit file, its blueprint exemption table, its
    16	comparator record and its artifact file set. The per-track data is §6; QPBT is
    17	the only track registered
    18	today, but nothing here is QPBT-specific.
    19	
    20	**Declaring finished** means any public statement that the track is complete: a
    21	completion comment on its umbrella issues (27/168 for QPBT), closing those
    22	issues, tagging a release, or a README/status page that says the track is done.
    23	
    24	## 2. Finished without caveat
    25	
    26	A track is finished without caveat at a commit when all seven criteria hold *at
    27	that commit*.
    28	
    29	**C1 — Proof integrity.** Zero term-level `sorry`, `admit`, project `axiom` or
    30	`constant` declaration, `native_decide` / `decide +native`, or
    31	`Lean.trustCompiler` under the track's Lean root. The sorry-site rule is the
    32	one in `results/telemetry/owner-tools/estimate.sh` (`SORRY_SITE_RE`), and there
    33	is exactly **one** implementation of it: `scripts/completion_gate.py` loads that
    34	line from that file and never restates it. Explicit axiom declarations are
    35	found with `DECL_RE` of `scripts/audit_lean_axiom_declarations.py`, imported
    36	rather than copied.
    37	
    38	**C2 — Headline axioms.** Every headline theorem of §6 depends only on
    39	`propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The check is a committed
    40	`AxiomAudit` Lean file for the track that carries one audit command per
    41	headline theorem — `assert_standard_axioms` (LDT) or `audit_standard_axioms`
    42	(the command QPBT's audit module defines); both print the axiom set and fail
    43	elaboration unless it is exactly those three — and is built in CI. The gate
    44	checks that the file
    45	exists and covers the table; the axiom values themselves come from the build
    46	and are reported as delegated.
    47	
    48	**C3 — Paper gaps terminal.** Every data row of the track's paper-gap register
    49	carries a `Terminal status` cell reading exactly `corrected` or
    50	`no-difference`:
    51	
    52	- `corrected` — a documented statement correction that **meets the four
    53	  adoption conditions of `local/protocols/issues-prs.md`** — correctness,
    54	  sufficiency, minimality ("the closest sufficient statement to the source,
    55	  with no unnecessary hypothesis or weakened conclusion and no change to the
    56	  source semantics") and Lean convergence — and carries its three artifacts: a
    57	  gap note, a corrected blueprint node citing it, and, where the printed claim
    58	  is not proved, the printed claim preserved as a non-asserted `Prop` (the
    59	  `lem:symmetric-strat` and `lem:qld-4-13` pattern of 2026-09-19). The
    60	  artifacts are evidence that a correction was adopted; they are not a route
    61	  around those conditions, and a row whose correction weakens a conclusion is
    62	  not terminal however complete its artifacts are.
    63	- `no-difference` — the formalization and the source statement agree; nothing
    64	  to correct.
    65	
    66	No row may read `open`, `pending` or `sorry`. No headline theorem statement may
    67	be weaker than the source paper except through a `corrected` row.
    68	
    69	**C4 — Blueprint marked.** Every blueprint node of the track that carries
    70	`\lean{...}` also carries `\leanok`, or appears in the track's exemption table
    71	with a written reason; `scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py --ci` exits 0. A
    72	node is any environment the repository's blueprint parser recognises: the gate
    73	reads that list out of `_TEX_ENV_BEGIN_RE` in `scripts/blueprint_lean_sync.py`
    74	instead of keeping its own, so an `example` or `remark` node with a Lean link
    75	counts exactly as a theorem does. Which nodes are the track's is read off the
    76	tree and not off section 6: besides the chapters registered there, the gate
    77	reads every other `.tex` beside them whose `\lean{...}` names a declaration
    78	under the track's Lean root, and judges those nodes too, so a node of the track
    79	that lives in a chapter shared with another track is in scope whether or not
    80	its chapter is listed. The
    81	exemption table is the only place a permanently unmarked node may live, and a
    82	row there is a caveat that must be defensible in the paper.
    83	
    84	**C5 — Lean comparator.** A comparator challenge exists covering every headline
    85	theorem; the in-repository expected challenge is free of regeneration drift
    86	(`scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py` for that track's expected copy
    87	passes in CI); and the track's comparator record (§6, `docs/comparator.md`)
    88	states the challenge repository, the library commit that repository last
    89	verified with the official `leanprover/comparator` (`permitted_axioms` limited
    90	to the three standard axioms, external kernel check enabled where the platform
    91	allows), and the expected-copy path. That verified commit must be an
    92	ancestor-or-equal of the commit being declared finished, with no Lean change to
    93	the statement closure in between — which is exactly what a passing drift check
    94	proves.
    95	
    96	The coverage half of C5 is decided against the challenge, never against the
    97	record alone. The record's `expected-challenge` must be exactly the expected
    98	copy §6 registers for the track, and every headline theorem of §6 must occur in
    99	that file or split challenge tree by its fully-qualified name — the name the assembler of
   100	`scripts/comparator/` writes for each declaration of the closure. A record that
   101	lists a headline theorem the registered expected copy never names fails C5:
   102	`covered-theorems` is written by hand in the same document, by the same session
   103	that wants to declare the track finished, so it may not be its own evidence.
   104	That the challenge *elaborates* to the same statements is the drift check and
   105	the comparator run, both delegated to CI.
   106	
   107	**C6 — Docs truthful.** No README, status page or estimate may advertise a
   108	nonzero open-site count once C1 holds. Every doc the track registers (§6) must
   109	exist: a registered doc that has been renamed or deleted fails C6 rather than
   110	being skipped, so the criterion can never report a green run over zero docs.
   111	
   112	**C7 — Artifact readiness.** "Done" means ready to be attached as an artifact
   113	to an ITP submission (owner, 2026-09-19), so every file such a submission needs
   114	is committed at the declared commit: the files §6 registers for the track —
   115	today `README.md`, `docs/QPBT-theorem-index.md`, `docs/DEVIATIONS.md`,
   116	`docs/ARTIFACT.md` and `LICENSE` — and the snapshot script
   117	`scripts/make_artifact.sh`. The gate checks that each of them exists and fails
   118	closed naming the missing ones; that the script *produces* a snapshot whose
   119	leak scan passes is a run, and is reported as delegated like C2, C4 and C5.
   120	A missing artifact file is main's to-do list, not a caveat that may be carried
   121	into a completion statement.
   122	
   123	## 3. Where the comparator challenge lives
   124	
   125	The challenge repository lives **outside** this repository and outside the
   126	umbrella repository: a separate repository of its own, as `LDT-comparator`
   127	already is for `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` (`docs/comparator.md`). Three
   128	reasons, in order of weight:
   129	
   130	1. *Validating Proofs* level 4 requires the statement to be written in a
   131	   trusted environment separate from the proof code. A challenge inside this
   132	   repository would be elaborated in the same environment it is meant to check.
   133	2. The challenge must depend on this library **pinned by commit**. A repository
   134	   cannot meaningfully pin a commit of itself, and the pin is the evidence C5
   135	   rests on.
   136	3. `Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-qpbt` is the umbrella repository and is not the main
   137	   session's to modify (`local/personas/main.md`).
   138	
   139	What stays here: the generator (`scripts/comparator/`), the expected copy, the
   140	drift check, and the comparator record. Creating the challenge repository is an
   141	action outside this repository and is therefore an **owner action**, not a main
   142	decision.
   143	
   144	## 4. Who enforces this
   145	
   146	The main session, or the acting main, **may not** post a completion statement
   147	on the track's umbrella issues, close them, or tag a release unless
   148	
   149	    python3 scripts/completion_gate.py check --track <track>
   150	
   151	exits 0 on the exact commit being declared, and the gate's output is attached
   152	to the completion comment. A gate run on any other commit is not evidence.
   153	
   154	A failing gate is **not an owner blocker**. It is main's to-do list: no owner
   155	inbox comment is filed for it, and the work it names is ordinary development.
   156	
   157	The gate is deliberately **not** part of the blocking PR CI: it would fail every
   158	PR until the comparator challenge exists. `local/bin/ci.sh` has no non-blocking
   159	step class — every step it records is blocking — so CI is left unchanged, and
   160	the gate is run by hand before a completion statement.
   161	
   162	## 5. The gate
   163	
   164	`scripts/completion_gate.py` is python3, standard library only, no network and
   165	no model call. `check --track <t> [--repo-root R] [--commit C] [--json]` prints
   166	one PASS/FAIL line per criterion with `file:line` evidence, and exits 0 only
   167	when every mechanically checkable criterion passes. Criteria with a half that
   168	needs a run the gate does not perform (C2 axiom values, C4 `--ci` run, C5 drift
   169	regeneration, C7 snapshot leak scan) print as
   170	`DELEGATED` once their static half holds — never as `PASS`, so no completion
   171	comment can quote a green line for a check nobody ran — while a failing static
   172	half is still `FAIL`. `DELEGATED` does not turn a failing run green and does
   173	not by itself make one green either: the delegated halves are read off the CI
   174	run of the same commit. Unit tests:
   175	`scripts/tests/test_completion_gate.py`.
   176	
   177	## 6. Registered tracks
   178	
   179	### QPBT
   180	
   181	| Field | Value |
   182	|---|---|
   183	| Lean root | `MIPStarRE/QPBT` |
   184	| Blueprint chapters | `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex` |
   185	| Paper-gap register | `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt-gap-register.md` |
   186	| Axiom audit | `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean` |
   187	| `\leanok` exemptions | `docs/completion/qpbt-leanok-exemptions.md` |
   188	| Comparator record | `docs/comparator.md`, block `track=qpbt` |
   189	| Expected challenge | `scripts/comparator/expected/qpbt` |
   190	| Truthful docs (C6) | `README.md` |
   191	| Artifact files (C7) | `README.md`, `docs/QPBT-theorem-index.md`, `docs/DEVIATIONS.md`, `docs/ARTIFACT.md`, `LICENSE` |
   192	| Artifact script (C7) | `scripts/make_artifact.sh` |
   193	| Umbrella issues | 27, 168 |
   194	
   195	Headline theorems (blueprint chapter `ch13_qpbt_test.tex`):
   196	
   197	| Lean name | Blueprint node |
   198	|---|---|
   199	| `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` | `thm:pauli` |
   200	| `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit` | `cor:pauli-binary` |
   201	| `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_spcc_value_one` | `lem:pauli-completeness` |
   202	| `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness` | `lem:ld-soundness` |
   203	
   204	The expected challenge is the split tree generated from
   205	`scripts/comparator/challenges/qpbt.json`: its root `Challenge.lean` and
   206	mirrored modules together must name all four headline declarations above.
   207	The gate reads every Lean file in that registered tree, checks coverage against
   208	the headline table rather than the hand-written comparator record, and still
   209	requires the record's expected-copy path to agree exactly. Comparator
   210	verification remains delegated evidence: the record must name a verified
   211	ancestor revision, the official run must permit only the three standard
   212	axioms, and the drift check must establish agreement at the completion commit.
   213	
   214	The `Blueprint chapters` row is the track's own chapters, read whole; it is
   215	not the whole of C4's scope. The gate also reads every other `.tex` file in
   216	those directories whose `\lean{...}` names a declaration under the track's
   217	Lean root and judges those nodes — today
   218	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch03_preliminaries.tex` carries one such QPBT node — so
   219	a chapter missing from the row above narrows nothing.
   220	
   221	Adding a track means adding its row set here and its entry in the gate's
   222	`TRACKS` registry, in one commit; a unit test reads this section and fails if a
   223	registry entry names a path these rows do not. That test reads every
   224	path-valued field of `Track` — every row above but the umbrella issues — and
